A21-15.label: Avant-Garde Short
A21-15.defn: A short of the first and postwar avant-garde built on dream, ritual, rhythm or the plastic image rather than story: Dada and cinéma pur, surrealist, trance and psychodrama, mythopoeic and underground films (Ballet Mécanique, Un Chien andalou, Meshes of the Afternoon, Scorpio Rising). Lyrical, landscape, structural, found-footage and video works have their own leaves.
A21-15.axis: by avant-garde movement in historical order: Dada and cinéma pur, surrealism, the trance film, the mythopoeic and underground film, then later dream shorts

new_leaves.label: Lyrical Film
new_leaves.breadth: Personal, first-person avant-garde shorts in the Brakhage line: the camera as the maker's eye, body and memory.
new_leaves.defn: An avant-garde short in which the camera renders the filmmaker's own seeing, body, household or devotion, with handheld, rhythmic or painted imagery and no story (Anticipation of the Night, Window Water Baby Moving, Fuses, Notebook, Pneuma). A film observing a place goes to Landscape Film.
new_leaves.axis: by era, with Stan Brakhage's large body of work as its own section

new_leaves.label: Landscape Film
new_leaves.breadth: Avant-garde shorts devoted to place: cities, land, water, weather and light observed through the camera.
new_leaves.defn: An avant-garde short whose subject is a place — a city, a stretch of land or water, the weather or light over time — observed rather than narrated (Fog Line, New York Portrait, Study of a River, Altiplano, Night Without Distance).
new_leaves.axis: by kind of place and method: city films, structural and durational landscapes, then land, water and light by era

new_leaves.label: Structural Film
new_leaves.breadth: Avant-garde shorts whose shape is set by a predetermined system or by the film material itself.
new_leaves.defn: An avant-garde short whose form is a predetermined structure or an exposure of the film material and apparatus — fixed frame, flicker, loop printing, rephotography, metric montage (Arnulf Rainer, The Flicker, Serene Velocity, Zorns Lemma, Berlin Horse).
new_leaves.aliases: structural-materialist film; metric film; flicker film
new_leaves.axis: by school: Austrian formal film, Warhol, American structural film, British and European structural-materialist film, Owen Land's parodies, then contemporary analog work

new_leaves.label: Found-Footage Film
new_leaves.breadth: Avant-garde shorts made by re-editing, reprinting or manipulating footage shot by others.
new_leaves.defn: An avant-garde short assembled from appropriated footage — newsreels, Hollywood films, home movies, archives — re-edited, optically reprinted or physically altered (Rose Hobart, A Movie, Free Fall, Passage à l'acte, Outer Space).

new_leaves.label: Video Art & Expanded Cinema
new_leaves.breadth: Artists' video, gallery moving-image works and expanded-cinema pieces.
new_leaves.defn: A short moving-image artwork made on video or for the gallery, or an expanded-cinema piece that works with projection, performance or installation (Vertical Roll, Global Groove, Line Describing a Cone, Semiotics of the Kitchen, How Not to Be Seen).
new_leaves.aliases: artists' video; artists' moving image; gallery film

A21-12.label: Documentary Short
A21-12.defn: A nonfiction short of the sound era observing people, work and social life at first hand — portraits, social observation and sport — not made as sponsored, scientific, political, poetic, essay, arts or ethnographic film (Le Sang des bêtes, Les Raquetteurs, Seven Up!, Talking Heads).
A21-12.axis: by era for portrait and social shorts, then sport

new_leaves.label: Political Documentary Short
new_leaves.breadth: Short militant, activist and social-issue documentaries.
new_leaves.defn: A documentary short made to argue, mobilise or bear witness on a political or social cause — militant and revolutionary newsreels, anticolonial and activist films, war and social-issue reportage (Misère au Borinage, Afrique 50, Now, Hanoi Tuesday 13th, The White Helmets).
new_leaves.aliases: militant film; activist documentary short; social-issue documentary short
new_leaves.axis: by era: interwar and postwar militant film, the 1960s revolutionary and Third Cinema shorts, the 1970s collectives, then later activism

new_leaves.label: Poetic Documentary Short
new_leaves.breadth: Short documentaries organised by rhythm, image and mood rather than argument: city symphonies and lyrical studies of place and labour.
new_leaves.defn: A documentary short shaped by visual rhythm, montage and mood instead of exposition — city symphonies, lyrical studies of landscape, seasons and work (Manhatta, Rain, À propos de Nice, Islands of Fire, Beginning).
new_leaves.axis: city symphonies first, then poetic documentary by era

new_leaves.label: Essay Film Short
new_leaves.breadth: Short first-person and reflective nonfiction films that think through images, memory and history.
new_leaves.defn: A nonfiction short that reflects in a personal, argumentative voice, working through memory, history and images themselves (Night and Fog, The House Is Black, Reassemblage, Isle of Flowers, History and Memory).
new_leaves.aliases: short essay film; video essay; film essay

new_leaves.label: Arts Documentary Short
new_leaves.breadth: Short documentaries about artists, writers, filmmakers, musicians and dancers and their work.
new_leaves.defn: A documentary short whose subject is an art, an artist or a performance — painting and sculpture, writers, cinema and filmmakers, music and dance (Henri Matisse, Guernica, Jazz Dance, Werner Herzog Eats His Shoe, Kazuo Ohno).
new_leaves.aliases: art documentary short; music documentary short; dance documentary

new_leaves.label: Ethnographic Short
new_leaves.breadth: Short fieldwork and ethnographic documentaries of ritual, craft and community life.
new_leaves.defn: A documentary short recording the ritual, craft or daily life of a community as ethnographic fieldwork (Trance and Dance in Bali, Les Maîtres fous, The Ax Fight, Gestes du repas).
new_leaves.aliases: ethnographic documentary short; visual anthropology short

A19-1.label: Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité
A19-1.defn: A documentary of the 1960s–80s observational movements, or by their founding filmmakers, made by watching events as they happen with lightweight sync-sound cameras, no narration and minimal intervention (Primary, Chronicle of a Summer, Titicut Follies, Salesman, Grey Gardens). Later observational films go to Institutional, Work & Labour, Family or Observational Documentary; a first-person or reflexive film goes to A19-5; a staged film to A19-7.
A19-1.axis: by national school, with Frederick Wiseman as his own section

new_leaves.label: Institutional Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: Observational documentaries (1990–) set inside a single institution: schools, hospitals, courts, prisons, parliaments, museums.
new_leaves.defn: An observational documentary made since 1990 that watches the daily working of one institution — a school, hospital, court, prison, campaign or museum — from inside (To Be and to Have, The Waiting Room, Starless Dreams, Boys State, De humani corporis fabrica).

new_leaves.label: Work & Labour Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: Observational documentaries (1990–) of work: factories, mines, farms, fishing, trades and offices.
new_leaves.defn: An observational documentary made since 1990 that follows people at work — in factories, mines, fields, kitchens or offices (Workingman's Death, Our Daily Bread, Machines, Honeyland, American Factory).

new_leaves.label: Family Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: Observational documentaries (1990–) of families, couples and private lives, often followed over years.
new_leaves.defn: An observational documentary made since 1990 that follows a family, a couple or a private life at close range, often over years (Love and Diane, Last Train Home, Three Sisters, The Wolfpack, Time).

new_leaves.label: Observational Documentary
new_leaves.breadth: Observational documentaries (1990–) of communities, neighbourhoods, borders and places.
new_leaves.defn: An observational documentary made since 1990 that watches a community, neighbourhood or place without narration or interview (Bread Day, En Construcción, 45365, Sacro GRA, Fire at Sea, Hale County This Morning, This Evening). Films centred on one institution, on work or on a family have their own leaves.
